clue.text: Subject to political power, people finally submit — that's putting it mildly

parts.note: to be subject to something is to be under it
the state is the political power of a nation
men means people in general

indicators.note: finally picks only the closing letter of the word submit

explanation.surface: Someone living under an oppressive regime is told to knuckle under, and the speaker shrugs it off with mild words.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is less serious than it really is amounts to putting it mildly.

clue.text: Original founder receives bill — that's not explained

indicators.note: receives says one piece takes another inside it
original read as inventive or novel signals that the letters of founder are made anew

parts.note: an account is a bill to be paid

explanation.surface: The first founder of a company gets an invoice, and nobody can say why.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Original' looks like an adjective on 'founder' but is the anagram signal: FOUNDER rearranged gives UN...EDFOR, which 'receives' ACCOUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left unexplained has never been accounted for, an idiom for lacking justification.

clue.text: Manage to catch fish up in trawl

indicators.note: in a down clue up says the whole assembled piece reads from bottom to top
to catch says the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: to tend something is to manage or look after it
the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A fisherman tries to land a catch hauled up in the trawl net.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragnet is a net dragged along the sea floor, a trawl in the fishing sense.

clue.text: Sail with two little boys

parts.note: Roy is a boy's name, given here in a short familiar form
Al is a short form of the boy's name Albert or Alan

explanation.surface: Someone goes sailing with a pair of young lads.
explanation.definitionFit: A royal is a small sail set above the topgallant on a square-rigged ship.

clue.text: Allow upwardly mobile English bookmaker a turn on ski slope

indicators.note: in a down clue upwardly mobile says the word moves up, read from bottom to top

parts.note: to let is to allow
St Mark made a book, the second Gospel, so is a book maker

explanation.surface: An Englishman on the rise lets a betting shop owner have a go on the piste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bookmaker' suggests a turf accountant; it is the evangelist Mark, maker of a Gospel book.
explanation.definitionFit: The telemark is a Norwegian skiing turn made with one ski advanced and the knee bent.

clue.text: Leaders of Trade Unions sometimes seem less enthusiastic for the struggle

indicators.note: leaders of says take the opening letter of each following word in turn

explanation.surface: Union bosses can appear half-hearted about the fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A tussle is a vigorous scuffle or contest, a kind of struggle.

clue.text: Fruit dessert I made once, disastrously

indicators.note: disastrously says the cooking went wrong, so the letters before it are scrambled

explanation.surface: A cook recalls a pudding they once made that went badly wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A macedoine is a mixture of chopped fruits or vegetables, often served as a fruit salad or jelly.

clue.text: Offensive rumour about honour

indicators.note: about says the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: noise can mean talk or rumour, as in making noises about something
OM, the Order of Merit, is a British honour

explanation.surface: A nasty piece of gossip concerns somebody's award.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means foul or disgusting, especially of a smell, so offensive.

clue.text: Source of music one listens to

definitions.text: Source of music one listens to

parts.words: Source of music one listens to
parts.note: read flatly any radio or record player fits; the hint is that only one person can listen, through headphones on a portable player

explanation.surface: A plain description of something that produces music for a listener.
explanation.definitionFit: A Walkman-style portable cassette or CD player with headphones is heard by one listener alone.

clue.text: Everyone is surrounding contrary gardener's plant

indicators.note: surrounding says the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: all means everyone
the nursery rhyme asks 'Mary, Mary, quite contrary, how does your garden grow?'
taken as written

explanation.surface: All the company gather round a perverse gardener's prize bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Amaryllis is a bulb grown for its large trumpet-shaped flowers, a garden or house plant.

clue.text: Man in church producing peal

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
him is the pronoun used for a man

explanation.surface: A bellringer in church produces a ring of bells.
explanation.definitionFit: A chime is a ringing sound of bells, much like a peal.

clue.text: In California, an artificial construction for boats

indicators.note: In says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Somewhere in California an engineered waterway is built for boats.
explanation.definitionFit: A canal is a man-made waterway dug to carry boats and barges.

clue.text: Honey not nice and sweet

parts.note: mel is Latin for honey, used in pharmacy
odious means hateful, far from nice

explanation.surface: A partner called Honey turns out unpleasant rather than sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Honey' reads as a term of endearment; it gives MEL, the Latin word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet describes pleasant-sounding music, which is tuneful in exactly that sense.

clue.text: Improper expression for "away from"?

definitions.meaning: toward means in the direction of, so with un- in front it jokingly reads as its opposite

explanation.definitionFit: Untoward means unseemly or inappropriate; split as un- plus toward it fancifully means moving away.

clue.text: Keen wife thought over annual holiday up North

parts.note: an idea is a thought
the wakes are annual holiday weeks in northern English mill towns

explanation.surface: An eager wife plans the yearly trip in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Wakes week was the annual summer shutdown of mills in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alert and eager, fully awake to opportunities, is to be keen.

clue.text: Responsibility of carrier of messages

definitions.meaning: a homing bird trained to fly back with notes

explanation.surface: Someone is in charge of the messenger.
explanation.definitionFit: A homing bird carries messages; the idiom 'not my pigeon' means not my concern.

clue.text: Forbidding obstacle that may be accepted as challenge

definitions.text: that may be accepted as challenge

parts.note: gaunt can mean grim and forbidding in appearance
a let is a hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: A daunting barrier is offered as a dare to be taken up.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing down a glove was a medieval challenge, and picking it up accepted the duel.

clue.text: Diatribe delivered by one engaged in marketing

indicators.note: engaged in says the first piece holds the second within it

parts.note: trade is buying and selling, marketing goods
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A salesperson launches into an angry rant.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long angry speech of denunciation, which is a diatribe.

clue.text: Put new life into and uplifted drudge confined by that woman

indicators.note: in a down clue uplifted says the whole piece reads bottom to top
confined by says the drudge is put inside the other piece

parts.note: her refers to that woman
a serf is a downtrodden labourer, a drudge

explanation.surface: A tired servant, kept down by his mistress, is revived and cheered up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifted' turns the whole container, not just the drudge: the answer is the full assembly read upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To refresh is to revive or reinvigorate, giving new life.

clue.text: Parting with vessel back in the autumn

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn

indicators.note: back says the word for the vessel is read from right to left

parts.note: a ewer is a large jug, a vessel

explanation.surface: A goodbye comes as a ship returns in the autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: A farewell is a goodbye, the act of parting.

clue.text: Unreliable fellow about to desert

indicators.note: about says the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: Eric is any man's name, a fellow
to rat is to desert, as a rat leaves a sinking ship

explanation.surface: An untrustworthy man is on the point of deserting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'on the point of'; 'about' is the container and 'to desert' gives RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic means unpredictable or inconsistent, so not to be relied upon.

clue.text: Allow the devil in — you'll never get rid of him

definitions.text: you'll never get rid of him

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to let is to allow
an imp is a little devil

explanation.surface: Let the devil in and he will never leave.
explanation.definitionFit: A limpet clings to rock, so a person who hangs on and cannot be shaken off is called one.

clue.text: Letting air out, floated in disarray

indicators.note: disarray says the letters of floated in are thrown into confusion

explanation.surface: Something that once floated is now collapsing in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in disarray' looks like one phrase; its 'in' is part of the fodder, and 'disarray' alone signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Deflation is the release of air from a tyre or balloon.

clue.text: Walk stiffly, with member resisting pressure

definitions.meaning: to walk in a stiff, self-important manner
a structural bar that takes compression in a framework

explanation.definitionFit: Strut is a proud stiff walk and also a brace in a frame bearing compressive load.

clue.text: Kid taken to court over offence, ultimately

parts.note: sued means taken to court

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of the word offence

explanation.surface: A child is prosecuted in the end for a misdemeanour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' reads as a child; it means the leather made from a young goat.
explanation.definitionFit: Kid leather from young goats is often finished with a napped surface, so kid can be suede.

clue.text: Conclusion derived from some games

indicators.note: derived from says the letters come straight out of the words some games

explanation.surface: A deduction is drawn from a few matches.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final letter of the Greek alphabet, hence the end or conclusion.

clue.text: Material bringing about conversion of proselyte

indicators.note: conversion of says the letters of proselyte are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A missionary's fabric comes from converting a new believer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conversion' suits a proselyte, a convert, but here it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Polyester is a synthetic fibre woven into cloth, a material.

clue.text: Applaud resoundingly

parts.note: a straight description of clapping so loudly that the noise rings back from the walls

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to cheer so loudly and long that the sound reverberates.
